questions.prompt: Which statement about helminths in general is FALSE?

options.text: Helminths can range from microscopic to macroscopic in size.
Their cuticle is made of collagen and chitin.
Most helminth species are harmful parasites.
The three major subgroups are Cestodes, Trematodes, and Nematodes.

questions.explanation: False. Most helminths are actually harmless; only some parasitic species cause disease.

questions.prompt: What structure does a tapeworm (Cestode) use to attach to its host?
What are proglottids, and why does their hermaphroditic nature matter for a tapeworm's reproduction?
questions.explanation: Proglottids are the repeating, identical segments that make up a tapeworm's body. Because each proglottid is hermaphroditic (contains both ovaries and testes), every single segment can independently produce eggs, dramatically increasing the worm's reproductive output.

questions.prompt: Which statement comparing Cestodes and Trematodes is FALSE?

options.text: Both have flat bodies with high surface area.
Trematodes attach to hosts using a scolex, just like Cestodes.
Cestodes are made of repeating segments called proglottids.
Most Trematodes are host- and organ-specific.

questions.explanation: False. Trematodes do NOT attach via a scolex or have proglottids; those are Cestode-specific features.

questions.prompt: Which characteristic distinguishes Nematodes from both Cestodes and Trematodes?
Why do blood-feeding helminths produce anticoagulants, and what is this a useful example of in terms of parasite adaptation?
questions.explanation: Blood-feeding helminths produce anticoagulants in their saliva to keep the host's blood flowing freely while they feed, preventing clots from cutting off their food source - a useful adaptation for maximizing feeding efficiency.

questions.prompt: Parasitic worms are being researched as a treatment for which of the following conditions?

options.text: Allergies, Crohn's disease, and Irritable Bowel Syndrome

questions.explanation: Allergies, Crohn's disease, and Irritable Bowel Syndrome.

questions.prompt: Mebendazole (Vermox) works as an antihelminthic by:

options.text: Inhibiting sugar absorption in the worm

questions.explanation: Inhibiting sugar absorption in the worm.

questions.prompt: What makes Caenorhabditis elegans valuable as a model research organism? Name at least two specific facts about its cell biology.
questions.explanation: C. elegans has exactly 959 cells in the adult (eutely), undergoes 131 programmed cell deaths during development, and has 302 interconnected neurons - this precise, mapped cell lineage and nervous system makes it extremely valuable for studying development, cell biology, and neuroscience.

questions.prompt: A mosquito transmitting malaria is an example of a:

options.text: Mechanical vector, because it just carries the parasite on its legs
Biological vector, because the pathogen reproduces inside the mosquito
Neither, since mosquitoes don't transmit disease

questions.explanation: Biological vector, because the pathogen reproduces inside the mosquito.

questions.prompt: A house fly landing on food after walking through waste, physically carrying bacteria on its body, is an example of a:
Explain the key difference between a mechanical vector and a biological vector, using one example of each.
questions.explanation: A mechanical vector transmits a pathogen by physically carrying it on its body parts, with no reproduction of the pathogen inside the vector (e.g., a house fly). A biological vector transmits a pathogen that actually reproduces inside the vector itself before being transmitted (e.g., a mosquito transmitting malaria).

questions.prompt: Which pairing of organism to disease/classification is FALSE?
questions.explanation: False. Dirofilaria causes heartworm infections (Dirofilariasis), not Guinea-worm disease (which is caused by Dracunculus).

options.text: How hookworm infection can suppress allergies
How to eliminate all parasitic worms from the human population
The genetic sequence of Caenorhabditis elegans

questions.explanation: How hookworm infection can suppress allergies.

questions.prompt: Describe the life cycle of Ascaris, from egg ingestion to adult worm, based on what this module covered.
questions.explanation: Eggs are ingested and hatch in the digestive tract; larvae enter blood vessels and travel to the lungs; the worms are then carried up the trachea and swallowed; adult worms grow and reproduce in the intestines.
